01 · The Brief
Econsave · Packaging Creation01 · The Brief
The engagement
Packaging design for two frozen processed-chicken SKUs produced by Huat Lai as OEM for the Econsave house range. Design only — the product, the plant and the pack format do not change.
What we are designing

Front and back artwork for two SKUs, standard flavour only. Three design directions per SKU on the real pack proportion, Econsave picks one, then two rounds of amendment and print-ready files to the converter.

What decides the design

Econsave has fixed two things: orange and green as the colour scheme, and an open window on the breaded nugget so the shopper sees the real product. Everything else is ours to propose.

Not in this scope

No new logo or identity. No range architecture. No flavour extensions — standard flavour only. No photography shoot, no plant or line changes, no retail POS. If the range grows later, that is a separate brief.

Why the names are locked

The printed product description has to match the halal certificate and the product registration. We set it in the layout, we do not re-word it. Both languages appear on the front panel, English and Bahasa Malaysia, and the Bahasa line is not smaller than half the English cap height.

Why the two faces are so different

SKU 1 is a wide short pouch, SKU 2 is a tall bag more than twice its area. The same two colours held in the same proportion across both faces is what makes them read as one Econsave range rather than two unrelated packs.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 01 · The BriefSource: Econsave OEM product sheet · Page 05
Econsave · Packaging Creation01 · The Brief
The design criteria
Econsave issued two design criteria. Both are narrow, and both settle large parts of the layout before a single concept is drawn.
Criterion 01 · Orange and green

Orange is the appetite colour of the fried and breaded category — it is what the eye reads as cooked, hot, crisp. Green in a freezer reads as fresh or better-for-you. Our position: orange carries the pack, green carries the trust — halal and certification marks, the vegetable garnish, the claim band and the cooking instructions. Never a fifty-fifty split; that reads as a supermarket flyer, not a product.

Criterion 02 · Open window

A window costs printable area and bag stiffness, so it has to earn its place. It sits low and centred where the nuggets settle, never across a seal, and never so wide that the bag loses structure. The printed area above the window does the selling — brand, product name, weight. The window does the proving.

01
The window sets the grid, not the other way around

On SKU 2 the window takes the lower half of the face. Brand block, product name and weight compress into the upper half, so the name works at a smaller cap height than it would on a fully printed bag. Every wireframe in section 05 is drawn from the window outward.

02
Two colours, one system, two very different faces

Holding the orange-to-green ratio constant across a landscape pouch and a portrait bag is what creates the block on the shelf. We fix the ratio in section 05 and apply it identically to both.

03
House brand means legible, not loud

Econsave competes on price and trust. Beside branded packs that are already busy, the value pack wins by being cleaner — fewer elements, larger, in a stricter grid. Restraint is the differentiator in this aisle.

02 · Market & Shelf
Econsave · Packaging Creation02 · Market & Shelf
The category
Malaysian frozen processed chicken — frankfurters and nuggets — sorts itself into four tiers. Econsave enters at the value tier, and the pack has to say so without looking cheap. PROPOSED
Tier 01 · Branded leader

Ayamas, Ramly. Strong equity, appetite photography, premium finish. The pack sells the brand first and the product second. Shoppers pay a premium for reassurance.

Reference point, not competitor
Tier 02 · Branded challenger

Farm’s Gold, Ayam Seri, Bestie Deli. Mid-price, busy layouts, heavy claim usage. Fighting for the same eye with more elements than they can afford.

Direct benchmark set
Tier 03 · House brand

Econsave — this project. Retailer-owned, price-led, produced by an OEM. Wins on trust in the retailer plus visible value. Must look like the store stands behind it.

Where we play
Tier 04 · Unbranded / bulk

Loose or plain vacuum packs, catering sizes, wet-market frozen. No pack story at all — sold on price per kilo alone.

The floor we must clear
What the tier means for the design

A house brand that copies the branded challengers loses — it looks like a cheaper version of them. A house brand that goes plainer and more organised reads as confident and honest, which is exactly what a value shopper is buying. Fewer elements, bigger, straighter.

Practical consequence: no gradient overload, no starburst, no five different typefaces. One brand block, one product name, one proof device (photograph or window), one weight, one claim strip.

Where the volume sits

Both SKUs are family-size, not single-serve: 300g of frankfurter is roughly 5–6 pieces, and 800g of nugget is a bag that lasts a household a week or more. That tells us the buyer is stocking up for a household, not buying a snack.

The pack should therefore look like a pantry staple — repeat-purchase, easy to find again — not like an impulse item.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 02 · Market & ShelfBy brandmethod.co · Page 09
Econsave · Packaging Creation02 · Market & Shelf
Who we are designing for
Three shopper types account for most of this volume in an Econsave store. Each one changes something specific on the pack. PROPOSED
Primary
The household stock-up

Mother or main grocery buyer, 28–50, buying for a family with school-age children. Comes in with a list, buys the large size, freezes it, and repeats the same purchase for months. Price-aware but not price-only — will not risk food the children refuse to eat.

SHE NEEDS: WEIGHT VISIBLE · HALAL VISIBLE · PRODUCT VISIBLE
Secondary
The young household

Working adults and young couples, 20–35, cooking fast on weeknights. Buys on convenience and price. Reads the cooking instruction before buying — air fryer time matters more than brand.

HE NEEDS: COOKING CUE · SPEED · A FAIR PRICE
Third
The small trade buyer

Warung, canteen, small café and home-based food seller buying at cash & carry. Buys by weight and by carton. Cares about consistency, piece count and cost per portion, not brand story.

HE NEEDS: NET WEIGHT · PIECE COUNT · CARTON CLARITY

Econsave · Packaging Creation02 · Market & Shelf
The two-second freezer door
The pack is seen through fogged glass, at an angle, alongside twenty near-identical orange and yellow bags. That is the real design problem — not the artwork on screen.
What actually happens

The shopper opens the door, the glass clears, and the eye lands on one element per pack before moving on. Whatever that element is, it must answer “what is this?”.

On the benchmark packs, that element is almost always the product photograph or the product itself, not the logo. The brands that lead with a logo lose the glance.

Frost, condensation and plastic reflection all reduce contrast. Fine type and mid-tone colours disappear. Dark type on a light field, or white type on a saturated field — nothing in between.

The reading order we design to
1
What is it

Product name, or the product seen through the window. Largest element on the face.

2
Can I buy it

Halal mark. A non-negotiable, and its absence ends the sale immediately.

3
Who made it

The Econsave brand block. Reassurance, not the hook.

4
How much

Net weight, isolated and bold, for the price comparison she is already doing.

The rule we hold every layout to

If you cannot identify the product, confirm it is halal and read the net weight from two metres away with the pack behind glass, the layout has failed — regardless of how it looks at full size on screen. Every wireframe in section 05 is tested at that distance before it is presented.

Econsave · Packaging Creation02 · Market & Shelf
The window, in practice
The back panels of the same three bags show how the window is actually executed on a pillow bag today, and where it goes wrong.
Ayam Seri · backWindow is a small rectangle low on the panel, half covered by the sealed lap. Product barely visible.
Ayam Pertiwi · backTall window down the centre, but the fin seal runs straight through it. The seam distorts the view.
Ramly · backNarrow centre window, printed panels either side. Clean, but the window is too small to prove anything.
Mistake 01 · The seal crosses the window

On a pillow bag the fin or lap seal runs vertically down the back. Any window crossing it is distorted and cloudy at exactly the point the shopper looks. Our window sits fully to one side of the seal, or the pack goes to a three-side seal format.

Mistake 02 · The window is too small to prove

A narrow slot shows two nuggets, not a bagful. The point of a window is volume — the shopper needs to see the mass of product she is paying for. Below roughly a third of the panel width it stops working.

What we do differently

Window on the front, not the back. Placed low where the nuggets settle so it is never half empty. Wide enough to show the mass. Clear of every seal, clear of the gusset, and clear of the tear notch by a margin the converter confirms.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 02 · Market & ShelfBy brandmethod.co · Page 14
Econsave · Packaging Creation02 · Market & Shelf
The Ayamas standard
Ayamas is the pack the whole Malaysian category is measured against. It is worth being precise about why it works, because the parts that make it work are all free.
Ayamas Premium Chicken Frankfurters 300g · art direction reference
Why it is the benchmark

It is the pack a Malaysian shopper already trusts in this category. Matching its discipline — not its finish — is the fastest way to make a new house brand look established.

01
One flat colour field, edge to edge

The whole face is a single saturated red. No gradient mesh, no background photograph, no texture. It makes an unmistakable colour block on the shelf and it prints cleanly on film in one pass.

02
The brand block sits top-centre and never moves

Same size, same position, same clear space on every SKU in the range. That consistency is what lets a shopper find the brand again in a crowded door.

03
A strict vertical hierarchy under the brand

Descriptor, then product name in English, then the Bahasa line, then the claim. Four steps, each visibly smaller than the one above. Nothing competes.

04
The serving photograph is a window, not a wallpaper

The food sits in a defined rectangle in the lower half, cropped tight, on a dark plate. It never bleeds behind the type, so the type never loses contrast.

05
All legal and certification marks live in one strip

Halal, MeSTI and the rest are lined up along the bottom edge in a single row at a single size — organised, not scattered. It reads as compliance, not clutter.

What we adopt for Econsave

All five, in orange and green instead of red. What we do not adopt is the premium finish — Ayamas earns its gloss and foil because it charges for it. A house brand that imitates a premium pack looks like a copy. We take the discipline and leave the decoration.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 02 · Market & ShelfBy brandmethod.co · Page 15
Econsave · Packaging Creation02 · Market & Shelf
What the shelf teaches
Six competitor packs, two categories, one conclusion: the aisle is full of packs that are busier than they need to be. That is the opening.
The pattern across all six
  • Every pack leads with orange or red. Green appears only as a trust or garnish cue, never as the field.
  • Net weight is always the smallest thing on the pack, despite being the number the shopper is comparing.
  • Legal copy, nutrition tables and ingredient lists appear on front panels where they compete with the sell.
  • Certification marks are scattered rather than aligned — which makes them read as decoration, not credentials.
  • The brand block position is inconsistent even within one brand’s own range.
The five moves that follow from it
01
Orange field, green trust

Orange owns the face. Green owns the certification strip, the claim band and the garnish. Fixed ratio, both SKUs.

02
Weight gets its own space

Isolated, bold, in a consistent corner. Free differentiation.

03
The front sells, the back informs — where there is a back

True on SKU 2. SKU 1’s back is transparent, so its compliance panel is designed into the front from the start.

04
One certification strip

All marks, one row, one height, along the bottom edge.

05
Prove the product

A window on the nugget. The frankfurter is already proven by its transparent back.

The position, in one line

The Econsave pack is the clearest pack in the door. Not the loudest, not the cheapest-looking — the one where you can tell what it is, that it is halal, and how much you get, before you have finished opening the door.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 03 · Art DirectionBy brandmethod.co · Page 18
Econsave · Packaging Creation03 · Art Direction
Route A · Product Hero
The food is the picture, and it fills the face. Ayamas, Carnex and Perdue all run this route — it is the category default, and it is the safest place for a new house brand to start.
Ayamas · flat red field, photograph in a defined rectangle
Carnex · single product rendered huge, gradient field behind
Perdue · product photograph plus a green claim band
What it does well

Instant category recognition — there is no ambiguity about what is in the bag. Appetite appeal is at its highest. It needs no explanation and no brand equity to work, which is exactly the position a new house brand is in.

What it costs

It needs real food photography, styled and shot, or a licensed library image good enough to enlarge. It is also the most crowded route — every competitor in the benchmark set is already doing it, so the pack risks disappearing into the block.

How we would differentiate it

Flat orange field with no gradient, photograph cropped into a hard-edged rectangle rather than floating, and a green certification strip along the bottom. On SKU 2 the window replaces the photograph entirely — the real product outperforms any picture of it.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 03 · Art DirectionBy brandmethod.co · Page 19
Econsave · Packaging Creation03 · Art Direction
Route B · Clean House
Restraint as the value signal. No Brand, Kindfull, Schaller & Weber and Smokey Denmark’s all say “we spent the money on the food, not the bag” — and they look more expensive for it.
No Brand · retailer house brand, one light field, one hero image
Kindfull · cream ground, flat icon, enormous white space
Schaller & Weber · clear film, one printed label, product does the work
Smokey Denmark’s · die-cut label on clear film, single colour
What it does well

It is the strongest route for a retailer house brand specifically — No Brand is the proof. Clean packs read as honest and self-assured, which is exactly what “the store stands behind this” needs to feel like. It also stands out hardest in a busy freezer, because everything around it is shouting.

Why it suits this brief

It is the cheapest to print — fewer colours, large flat areas, no photographic mid-tones to hold on film. It is also the closest fit to the pack we already have: SKU 1 is a printed front on a transparent back, which is the Schaller & Weber label-on-clear-film idea exactly, and on SKU 2 the window does the same job.

What it risks

In a Malaysian value aisle a very quiet pack can read as unbranded or imported. The guard is a strong, unmistakable Econsave block and a saturated orange element carrying the face — clean, but not pale.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 03 · Art DirectionBy brandmethod.co · Page 20
Econsave · Packaging Creation03 · Art Direction
Route C · Flat Illustration
Drawn rather than photographed. Proty, Dino Buddies, Beggin’ and Vilniaus all build the face from flat colour and illustration — the most ownable route, and the most family-friendly.
Proty · flat colour, mascot, flavour coded by pack colour
Dino Buddies · character-led, aimed straight at children
Beggin’ · flat yellow field, illustration plus a real product window
Vilniaus · flat colour blocks, illustrated serving suggestion
What it does well

It is the only route that is genuinely ownable — an illustration style cannot be bought from a stock library by the competitor next door. It also speaks directly to the household buyer with children, which is our primary shopper.

What it costs

Illustration has to be commissioned and it has to be good; a weak drawing looks cheaper than a weak photograph. It also carries a risk of reading as a children’s snack rather than a family staple, which would narrow the shopper base.

How we would hold it

Flat orange and green only, no shading. Illustration used for the garnish and the cooking cue, not for the product — the product is proven by the window on SKU 2 and the transparent back on SKU 1. Grown-up typography keeps it a family pack, not a kids’ pack.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 03 · Art DirectionBy brandmethod.co · Page 21
Econsave · Packaging Creation03 · Art Direction
What we take, what we leave
Across all eleven references, this is what carries into the Econsave packs regardless of which direction is chosen — and what stays on the board.
Take — into all three directions
  • One flat colour field. No gradient meshes, no photographic backgrounds. It blocks on shelf and prints in fewer passes.
  • A fixed brand block position. Top of the face, same size and clear space on both SKUs, never moved.
  • A hard-edged image or window area. Product shown inside a defined shape, never floating and never bleeding behind type.
  • One aligned certification strip along the bottom edge, single row, single height.
  • Net weight isolated in its own corner, larger than every competitor sets it.
Leave — on the reference board
  • Premium finishes. Foil, gloss varnish, embossing. A house brand that looks expensive undermines its own price argument.
  • Character mascots as the lead device. Reads as a children’s snack; our primary buyer is stocking a family freezer.
  • Nutrition callout badges on the front. The Perdue-style badge cluster is regulated differently in Malaysia and it clutters the two-metre read.
  • Flavour-coded pack colours. Standard flavour only in this scope — a colour-coding system with nothing to code is dead weight.
  • Script and vintage lettering. Poor legibility behind fogged glass at distance.
How this feeds section 06

The three design directions presented later in this book are Route A, Route B and Route C, each built on the same wireframe, the same colour ratio and the same pack specification. That is deliberate: it means Econsave is choosing a look, not re-choosing the layout, the sizes or the compliance work. Whichever direction is picked, the engineering underneath it is already agreed.

Window dieRounded rectangle, radius 6 mmPROPOSED
The one thing that must be checked first

On a pillow bag the fin seal runs down the back. A window placed centrally on the flat sheet can end up crossing that seal — exactly the fault visible on two of the three benchmark bags. The position here is set to clear it, but the converter must confirm against their former and sealing jaws.

Why it sits low: frozen nuggets settle to the bottom in transit. A window in the upper half shows an empty bag by the time it reaches the freezer door.

Econsave · Packaging Creation04 · Pack Specification
Window geometry
The window is the one thing Econsave specified that changes the engineering of the pack, not just its appearance. These are the clearances we design to, and the three shapes available. PROPOSED
Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 04 · Pack SpecificationBy brandmethod.co · Page 26
Econsave · Packaging Creation04 · Pack Specification
Material, print & compliance
What has to be true of the film and the press before artwork is finalised, and what has to appear on the pack by law. Nothing here is a design choice — it is the frame the design has to fit.
Material · to confirm
  • Film structure — laminate layers and thickness, and whether the window is a clear panel in the laminate or a die-cut with a separate clear ply.
  • Freezer performance — the film must stay flexible at −18 °C without the print cracking on the fold.
  • Seal integrity — the window edge must survive the drop test at carton weight.
Print · to confirm
  • Process — rotogravure or flexo. Flexo limits fine reversed type and small screen percentages.
  • Colour count — how many stations. Two spot colours plus black is our target; it keeps cost down and colour consistent between runs.
  • Minimum type size and minimum reversed rule weight the press can hold on this film.
  • Registration tolerance — decides whether we can butt two colours or must trap them.
Compliance · must appear
  • Product name in Bahasa Malaysia and English.
  • Net weight in metric.
  • Full ingredient list in descending order, with allergens declared.
  • Nutrition information panel.
  • Manufacturer name and address; “Product of Malaysia”.
  • Halal certification mark, storage instruction and cooking instruction.
  • Batch code and expiry date field, left clear for the on-line coder.
  • EAN-13 barcode, with quiet zone respected.
The coder window — the detail that is always missed

Batch and expiry are printed on the line by a thermal or laser coder after the bag is made. That coder needs a clear, light, unvarnished strip of a fixed size in a fixed position, and it will print straight over whatever artwork is underneath it. We reserve it in the wireframe rather than discovering it at press — on two of the six benchmark packs the code is printed across the brand name, and that is why.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 04 · Pack SpecificationBy brandmethod.co · Page 27
05 · Wireframe Variations
Econsave · Packaging Creation05 · Wireframe Variations
How to read these pages
A wireframe fixes where things go and how big they are. It carries no colour, no typeface and no imagery — those come in section 06. Agreeing the wireframe first is what stops a colour argument from re-opening the layout.
Anatomy of a wireframe page
What you are looking atWhat it means
Dashed orange outlineBleed. Artwork must extend to here so nothing white shows if the film shifts on the press.
Solid dark outlineThe trim — the finished edge of the pack face.
Grey bandsSeal areas. Nothing important is placed here; the film is welded and distorted.
Solid dark blockThe Econsave brand block. Same size and position on both SKUs in every variation.
Peach blockThe open window — the physical die-cut. There is no artwork here at all.
Dashed grey blocksType and image areas. The box is the space the element gets; the design fills it.
Green stripCertification strip — one row, one height, along the bottom edge on every variation.
What we need back from this section

One decision: which of the three wireframes goes forward. Once that is chosen, all three design directions in section 06 are built on it, so the layout stops moving and only the look is still open. If none of the three is right, that is a useful answer too — it is far cheaper to redraw a wireframe than to redraw finished artwork.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 05 · Wireframe VariationsBy brandmethod.co · Page 29
Econsave · Packaging Creation05 · Wireframe Variations
AWindow Low
SKU 2 · chicken nugget. The category-standard layout, executed properly. Everything reads top to bottom in one column, and the window takes the bottom 40% of the face. PROPOSED
SKU 2 · window 192 × 116 mm, lower face
The idea

A single centred column. Brand block, product name in both languages, weight, then the window. It is how Ayamas, Ramly and Ayam Seri all organise their faces — the difference is that here the window replaces the photograph, and the weight gets real size instead of being tucked into a corner.

Strengths
  • Instantly familiar — nothing for the shopper to decode.
  • Widest possible window, so the product mass reads from furthest away.
  • Type sits entirely above the window, so no artwork is ever lost to the die-cut.
  • Translates to SKU 1 almost unchanged.
Trade-offs
  • It is the safest layout, so it is also the least distinctive on a shelf of the same layout.
  • The upper half has to carry brand, two languages, weight and a claim in 42 mm of height.
  • Relies entirely on colour and typography to stand apart.
Best paired with

Route A · Product Hero or Route B · Clean House. Both need a calm, conventional grid underneath them, and this is that grid.

Two-metre test

Passes. The window carries the identification on its own; brand and weight are read second, at closer range, exactly as intended.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 05 · Wireframe VariationsBy brandmethod.co · Page 30
Econsave · Packaging Creation05 · Wireframe Variations
BSplit Face
SKU 2 · chicken nugget. A vertical split: all the type in a left column, a tall window down the right. The most distinctive of the three, and the most demanding to execute. PROPOSED
SKU 2 · window 92 × 198 mm, right column
The idea

Break the category’s centred symmetry. Type stacks down the left in a strict column — brand, product name, weight, cooking icons — while the window runs floor to ceiling on the right. The pack reads as a label plus a view of the product, which is exactly the Schaller & Weber and Smokey Denmark’s idea from the art direction board, adapted to a bag.

Strengths
  • Nothing else in the benchmark set looks like this — strongest differentiation of the three.
  • Gives the product name far more height than variation A.
  • Room for the cooking icon set on the front, which the young-household shopper actually reads.
  • Tall window suits a bag that is stood upright in a freezer basket.
Trade-offs
  • A tall window shows an emptier bag — nuggets settle low, so the top third may look sparse.
  • A vertical die-cut on a pillow bag needs careful clearance from the side folds.
  • Harder to translate onto SKU 1’s wide, short face.
Best paired with

Route B · Clean House. The split only works if the left column is genuinely restrained; a busy left column turns it into two competing packs.

Two-metre test

Passes, but on the type rather than the product. Check a real filled bag before committing — if the window sits half-empty in the freezer, this variation loses its argument.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 05 · Wireframe VariationsBy brandmethod.co · Page 31
Econsave · Packaging Creation05 · Wireframe Variations
CArch Hero
SKU 2 · chicken nugget. A masthead band across the top, and a shaped arch window taking more than half the face. The window is not a feature of this pack — it is the pack. PROPOSED
SKU 2 · arch window 192 × 163 mm, radius 6 mm min
The idea

A full-width colour band across the top carries the brand, reversed out. Under it, the product name in both languages on a single line each. Everything below is window. The weight sits in a green roundel breaking into the window’s top corner, which is the only element allowed to overlap.

Strengths
  • The largest window of the three — maximum proof, maximum appetite.
  • The masthead band is a strong, repeatable range device: same band, different product name, and a third SKU drops straight in later.
  • Least artwork to produce, so the cheapest to print and the fastest to amend.
Trade-offs
  • An arch needs a new die — cost and lead time to confirm with the converter.
  • Very little printed area left for claims or a cooking cue; those move to the back.
  • The pack depends completely on the product looking good through the film. Poor breading or heavy frost is fully exposed.
  • It does not carry SKU 1 — with that pouch’s compliance panel on the front, an arch leaves too little printed area. SKU 1 would run wireframe A or B instead.
Best paired with

Route C · Flat Illustration. The band and the arch are graphic shapes, and flat illustration is the only route that treats them as such rather than fighting them.

Two-metre test

Strongest of the three — a solid mass of orange breaded product behind a shaped opening is the clearest signal available in this category. Conditional on the die being approved.

Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 05 · Wireframe VariationsBy brandmethod.co · Page 32
Econsave · Packaging Creation05 · Wireframe Variations
SKU 1 · the two that fit
The frankfurter pouch has a transparent back. The product proves itself through the pack, so there is no window on the front — and every legally required element has to fit on the printed front instead. TO CONFIRM
A · StackedSell across the top — brand, both product names, weight — then ingredients and nutrition side by side as a band, with the barcode and certification strip along the foot. Reads in the same top-to-bottom order as SKU 2.
B · ColumnSell down the left, compliance in a full-height column on the right. The taller column takes more body copy at a legible size, and it leaves room for a cooking cue on the front.
Why the third layout is gone

Variation C on SKU 2 gives its lower half to an arch window. With no window on this pouch and the whole compliance panel to place, C leaves the least printed area of the three and the ingredient text falls below a legible size. It cannot carry this SKU, so it is not offered here.

Whichever wireframe Econsave picks for SKU 2, SKU 1 runs A or B. The brand block, colour ratio and certification strip are identical either way, so the two packs still read as one range.

What the transparent back changes
  • No window, no die-cut, no extra tooling on this SKU. The pack is already see-through where it matters.
  • The whole compliance panel moves forward — ingredients, allergens, nutrition, manufacturer, storage, barcode, certification marks.
  • That is roughly half the front spoken for before the design starts, which is exactly why all three competitor fronts look crowded.
  • The coder strip for batch and expiry still needs a light, unvarnished reserve — on this pack it sits on the front, not the back.
Econsave Packaging Creation Book v1.0 · 05 · Wireframe VariationsBy brandmethod.co · Page 33
Econsave · Packaging Creation05 · Wireframe Variations
The back panel · SKU 2
This is the SKU 2 back panel — the nugget bag is printed on both sides. It serves all three variations unchanged. SKU 1 has a transparent back and carries the same elements on its front instead, on page 33. PROPOSED
Back panel · SKU 2 only · SKU 1’s back is transparent
Why it is fixed across all variations

The back carries no persuasion. Locking it now means the three design directions in section 06 differ only on the front — which halves the artwork, halves the amendment rounds, and removes any risk of a compliance element being dropped when a direction changes. The same element list applies to SKU 1, simply relocated to its printed front.

Reading order
  • Product name, so the bag is identifiable if it is stacked face down.
  • Cooking instructions — the most-read element on the back. Icons first, words under.
  • Nutrition and ingredients side by side, equal width.
  • Storage, then manufacturer.
  • Barcode and coder window, bottom.
Non-negotiable clearances
  • Barcode on a white ground with its quiet zone clear, never over colour or a fold.
  • Coder window unvarnished, light, fixed position, clear of all artwork.
  • Minimum body text size set by the press — to confirm.
  • Nothing within 10 mm of the fin seal.
Still needed

Final ingredient and nutrition copy from Huat Lai QA. The panel is laid out to real text, not placeholder — word count changes the panel size, and the panel size changes the rest of the back.

Zone rules
Rules that hold across every variation and both SKUs. If a design direction breaks one of these, the direction changes — not the rule.
#ZoneRuleWhy
01Brand blockTop of the face, same width and clear space on both SKUs. Never rotated, never below the product name, never smaller than 26 mm wide.Consistent position is how a shopper finds the range again at repeat purchase.
02Product nameEnglish first, Bahasa Malaysia directly under at no less than half the English cap height. Both above the window. Never reversed out of a photograph.Legal requirement and the primary identifier at two metres.
03Net weightIts own element, isolated, minimum 14 mm cap height on SKU 2 and 10 mm on SKU 1. Never inside a paragraph.It is the number the shopper compares against price. Every competitor buries it.
04Window / clear panelClear of all seals, folds and the tear notch by the margins on page 26. No printing inside it. Corner radius 6 mm minimum.Structural integrity and an honest view of the product.
05Certification stripOne row along the bottom edge, all marks at a single height, evenly spaced, on the green ground.Aligned marks read as credentials; scattered marks read as clutter.
06Halal markAlso appears on the front panel, in the certification strip. Never smaller than 8 mm.It is the first thing checked and its absence ends the sale.
07Coder windowReserved, unvarnished, light ground, fixed position on the back. No artwork underneath.The line coder prints over whatever is there.
08Colour ratioOrange dominant, green supporting, in the proportion fixed in section 06. Applies identically to both SKUs.A constant ratio across two very different faces is what creates the range block on shelf.
09The front sells, the back informs — on SKU 2No nutrition table, ingredient list or address block on the SKU 2 front panel. SKU 1 is the exception: its back is transparent, so the compliance panel is designed into the front as a defined zone, never squeezed into leftover space.Front-panel clutter is the biggest weakness in the benchmark set — but on a transparent-backed pouch it is unavoidable, so it gets planned rather than improvised.

The colour system
Orange and green, as Econsave specified. What was not specified is the ratio — and the ratio is what decides whether the pack looks like a product or like a promotion. PROPOSED
Econsave Orange

The ratio, fixed on both SKUs
65% ORANGE22% NEUTRAL13% GREEN

Orange carries the face. Neutral — white, the clear window, or the light ground in Direction 02 — gives the type room to breathe. Green appears only where it means trust: the certification strip, the claim band, the garnish.

Never a fifty-fifty split. Two colours at equal weight have no hierarchy, and a pack with no hierarchy reads as a supermarket flyer rather than a product.

Rules that survive the press
  • Two spot colours plus black is the target. It holds colour consistent between print runs and keeps the plate count — and the cost — down.
  • No gradients in the orange field. A flat field prints identically every run; a gradient shifts between runs and between converters.
  • Green never runs behind the product name. Green and orange at similar values vibrate against each other at distance.
  • All Pantone references are proposed and must be matched on the actual film — the same ink reads differently on white-backed and clear laminate.
  • A press proof on the real substrate is signed before the full run. Screen colour is never the reference.

Typography
One typeface family, four sizes, no exceptions. On a face this small, every additional weight or size costs legibility that the pack cannot spare. PROPOSED

Compliance bodyMinimum set by the press — TO CONFIRM
The rules
  • One family only. A grotesque with a true bold and a genuinely readable regular. No display face, no script, no condensed variant.
  • Caps for product names, sentence case for everything else. Caps read faster at distance; sentence case reads faster up close.
  • Never reverse small type out of a photograph or out of the orange field below 5 mm. Behind fogged glass it disappears.
  • Cap heights are specified in millimetres, not points — the two SKUs are different sizes, so point values would not be comparable.
Licensing

The final typeface must be licensed for commercial packaging and unlimited print run. We confirm the licence before it goes into artwork, not after.
